text:
nina: quick PSA: ran into a surprising deadline propagation mismatch between Retrofit suspend adapters and OkHttp's per-call timeouts in the Kotlin SDK sample app on Android 12/13. Repro & fix below.

omar: tl;dr?

nina: our UI cancels a coroutine scope after 2s (user nav away). Retrofit suspend wrapper was using a blocking `execute()` inside `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` (old pattern). We then relied on call.timeout(2, TimeUnit.SECONDS) on OkHttp to bound network time, but when coroutine cancelled the underlying OkHttp call kept running until its ReadTimeout fired (~10s). App experienced leaked background work and duplicate retries from our retry scheduler.

zach: so coroutine cancellation didn't cancel OkHttp call?

nina: exactly. Two separate timeout surfaces: coroutine job cancellation and OkHttp call timeout. If you only set OkHttp call.timeout and don't wire coroutine cancellation into the call, the coroutine may resume or continue waiting and your retry logic can kick in unexpectedly.

kat: can you paste the problematic helper?

nina: snippet: 
```kotlin
suspend fun <T> Call<T>.awaitOld(): Response<T> = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
  return@withContext execute() // blocking; doesn't observe coroutine cancellation
}
// elsewhere: call.timeout(2, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
```

omar: managed to reproduce in the sample app?

nina: yes. Test: 1) set call.timeout(2s), 2) server delays response 8s, 3) coroutine scope cancelled at 2s. Result: UI thinks cancelled but OkHttp call keeps running until 8s and our retry scheduler (bound to coroutine) sometimes re-issues duplicates because we didn't cancel the underlying call.

zach: what's the correct pattern?

kat: recommended approach: use suspendCancellableCoroutine or use OkHttp's `Call.timeout()` and also call.cancel() on coroutine cancellation. Example: 
```kotlin
suspend fun <T> Call<T>.awaitCancellable(): Response<T> = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
  cont.invokeOnCancellation { cancel() }
  enqueue(object: Callback {
    override fun onResponse(call: Call, resp: Response) { if (cont.isActive) cont.resume(resp) }
    override fun onFailure(call: Call, e: IOException) { if (cont.isActive) cont.resumeWithException(e) }
  })
}
```

omar: also mention okHttp call.timeout vs call.cancel interplay: call.timeout only triggers an internal timeout after configured duration; it does not auto-cancel when coroutine job is cancelled. So we must cancel the call explicitly on coroutine cancellation.

nina: patched sample app to use awaitCancellable everywhere, updated retry scheduler to check `call.isCanceled()` before cloning, and added a test that cancels the coroutine at 2s and expects no duplicate server requests. Branch and PR created.

zach: add docs: "Deadline propagation: tie coroutine cancellation to OkHttp call.cancel() and prefer enqueue + suspendCancellableCoroutine over blocking execute()." Include a small migration note for older sample code.

kat: also add runbook note for on-call: symptoms: UI reports cancel, but server shows continued long-running requests; metrics show unexpected retries after cancellation. Look for thread stacks in blocked socket read and logs where coroutine job was cancelled but call still active.

nina: will tweak test timings. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
